title: the coding toolset: what the model can actually do to a project
intent: The registry had one tool, and it ignored its own arguments. An agent that cannot read a file, find a file, change a line safely, run a command and hear what the command said is a chat window, not a harness. This wave is the vertical slice of a coding agent: real file discovery, real guarded editing, real asynchronous processes with bounded output, real Emacs introspection — all through the same registry and the same permission rules, so that the model never gets a capability the person does not have.
checks: ./scripts/dev ert tests/unit/test-yeah-result.el tests/unit/test-yeah-files.el tests/unit/test-yeah-edit.el tests/unit/test-yeah-process.el tests/unit/test-yeah-emacs.el tests/unit/test-yeah-tools.el tests/unit/test-yeah-undo.el
objection: A tool set that works when the agent is driven by a test is not a tool set that works when the agent is driven by a model: the model writes arguments it did not read twice, and a guarded edit that rejects everything is a wall, not a guard.
refuted_by: A model-driven task — read a small project, reproduce a failing test, edit it, rerun the test — that stops at the first refusal. The guard then costs more than the unguarded edit would have.
